title: Module 8 · Codes and Resuscitation
intro: Adult arrest drugs and timing, reversible causes (hyperkalemia, torsades, opioids, local anesthetic toxicity, tricyclics), bradycardia, adenosine, anaphylaxis, malignant hyperthermia and post arrest care.

cases.title: Asystole: the first drug
cases.stem: You arrive at a code. Rhythm: asystole. CPR is in progress, IV in place.

steps.q: What drug and when?

options.t: Epinephrine 1 mg IV as soon as possible, then every 3 to 5 minutes
Amiodarone 300 mg
Atropine 1 mg
options.why: Atropine is no longer in the arrest algorithm.

steps.q: What is your job during the code?

options.t: Call out epinephrine timing ("Epi due in one minute")
Prepare the next doses and ask about reversible causes (H's and T's)
Confirm weight and allergies, and help document drugs and times
Run the code
options.why: The code leader runs the code; you run the medications.

cases.pearl: **Asystole or PEA: epinephrine 1 mg now, every 3 to 5 minutes.**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)

cases.title: VF: shock first
cases.stem: VF. Two shocks given, still VF.

steps.q: When does epinephrine go in for VF?

options.t: After the initial defibrillation attempts fail (commonly after the second shock), then every 3 to 5 minutes
Before the first shock

steps.q: Still VF after the third shock. Which antiarrhythmic?

options.t: Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO push, then 150 mg if needed
Lidocaine 1 to 1.5 mg/kg, then 0.5 to 0.75 mg/kg
Adenosine 6 mg

steps.q: Are calcium, bicarbonate or magnesium routine in arrest?

options.t: No: only for specific causes (hyperkalemia, torsades, tricyclic overdose)
Yes, every code

cases.pearl: **VF: shock, epi after shocks fail, amiodarone 300 then 150 (or lidocaine).**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)

cases.title: Hyperkalemia arrest
cases.stem: A dialysis patient who missed two sessions arrests (PEA). K was 7.8 an hour ago.

steps.q: What do you have ready?

options.t: Calcium chloride 1 g IV (or calcium gluconate 3 g)
Regular insulin 10 units IV with dextrose 25 g
Sodium bicarbonate 50 mEq if acidotic
Amiodarone 300 mg

cases.pearl: **Hyperkalemia arrest: calcium, insulin + dextrose, bicarbonate if acidotic.**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)

cases.title: Torsades
cases.stem: Polymorphic VT with a long QT on methadone and ondansetron. Pulseless.

steps.q: Which drug besides defibrillation?

options.t: Magnesium sulfate 1 to 2 g IV push (in arrest)
options.why: Magnesium stabilizes the heart in torsades.

options.t: Procainamide

steps.q: After ROSC, what do you do with the med list?

options.t: Stop QT prolonging drugs, check and replace K and Mg, and use CredibleMeds to review the list
Nothing

cases.pearl: **Torsades: magnesium 1 to 2 g. Then stop QT drugs and fix K and Mg.**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)

cases.title: Opioid overdose
cases.stem: An unresponsive patient on a PCA with RR 4, pinpoint pupils, pulse present.

steps.q: What do you recommend?

options.t: Ventilate (bag mask) and give naloxone 0.4 mg IV, repeating or increasing as needed (up to 2 mg); 4 mg intranasal if no IV
options.why: Breathing support first; small IV doses avoid severe withdrawal in opioid dependent patients.

options.t: Wait to see if they wake up

steps.q: Why might naloxone wear off before the opioid?

options.t: Naloxone lasts about 30 to 90 minutes; many opioids last longer, so repeat doses or an infusion may be needed
options.why: Keep monitoring after the patient wakes.

options.t: It never wears off

cases.pearl: **Opioid OD: breathe for them, naloxone 0.4 mg IV and repeat. Watch for it wearing off.**

sources.t: AHA 2023 focused update on adult ACLS (toxicology and drug use)

cases.title: Local anesthetic toxicity
cases.stem: Minutes after a bupivacaine nerve block, a 70 kg patient seizes and then develops wide complex bradycardia.

steps.q: What is the antidote and dose?

options.t: Lipid emulsion 20%: 1.5 mL/kg (105 mL) bolus over 2 to 3 minutes, then 0.25 mL/kg/min
Naloxone

steps.q: How does epinephrine change in this arrest?

options.t: Smaller doses: 1 mcg/kg or less
options.why: ASRA: high dose epinephrine can worsen the outcome.

options.t: Double the usual dose

cases.pearl: **LAST: lipid 20% 1.5 mL/kg, then 0.25 mL/kg/min. Small epi doses.**

sources.t: Neal JM, et al. Third ASRA practice advisory on local anesthetic systemic toxicity. Reg Anesth Pain Med 2018;43:113-123

steps.q: What do you recommend?

options.t: Sodium bicarbonate 1 to 2 mEq/kg IV, repeat to narrow the QRS
Procainamide

sources.t: AHA 2023 focused update on adult ACLS (toxicology and drug use)

cases.title: Symptomatic bradycardia

steps.q: First drug?

options.t: Atropine 1 mg IV every 3 to 5 minutes, max 3 mg
Adenosine

steps.q: No response. Next options?

options.t: Epinephrine infusion 2 to 10 mcg/min, dopamine 5 to 20 mcg/kg/min, or pacing
Metoprolol

cases.pearl: **Brady: atropine 1 mg (max 3), then epi drip, dopamine or pacing.**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)

cases.title: Adenosine for SVT
cases.stem: Stable narrow complex SVT at 190. The patient has a central line.

steps.q: How is adenosine given?

options.t: Rapid IV push followed immediately by a saline flush
Slow over 2 minutes
options.why: It would be destroyed before reaching the heart.

steps.q: What dose with a central line?

options.t: 3 mg first (instead of 6 mg)
options.why: Also for heart transplant and dipyridamole or carbamazepine. Caffeine and theophylline blunt the effect.

options.t: 12 mg first
options.why: Too much through a central line.

cases.pearl: **Adenosine: fast push and flush. 6 then 12; 3 mg if central line, transplant, dipyridamole.**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)

cases.title: Anaphylaxis
cases.setting: Infusion center · after the first dose
cases.stem: Five minutes into an IV antibiotic: hives, wheeze, BP 80/45.

steps.q: First drug and route?

options.t: Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM (1 mg/mL) in the outer thigh, repeat every 5 to 15 minutes
options.why: Antihistamines and steroids are add ons, not first line.

options.t: Diphenhydramine 50 mg IV first
options.why: Does not treat airway or shock.

options.t: Epinephrine 1 mg IV push (cardiac arrest dose)
options.why: IV push 1 mg in a patient with a pulse can cause arrhythmia and severe hypertension.

steps.q: Not responding to IM doses. Next?

options.t: Epinephrine infusion and fluids, with the team
More diphenhydramine

cases.pearl: **Anaphylaxis: epi 0.5 mg IM thigh. Never 1 mg IV push when there is a pulse.**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)

cases.title: Malignant hyperthermia
cases.stem: Rising end tidal CO2, rigidity and fever after succinylcholine and sevoflurane.

steps.q: What is the drug and dose?

options.t: Dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg IV, repeated until signs resolve
Acetaminophen

steps.q: What pharmacist detail matters most?

options.t: Knowing where the MH cart is and which product you stock (Ryanodex reconstitutes much faster than Dantrium)
options.why: Dantrium takes many vials and time.

options.t: None

cases.pearl: **MH: dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg, repeat. Know your cart.**

sources.t: NYSORA: updated guidelines for managing malignant hyperthermia (MHAUS based)

cases.title: After ROSC
cases.stem: Pulse is back after VF arrest. Comatose. BP 82/48.

steps.q: Which targets are common?

options.t: SBP at least 90 and MAP at least 65; norepinephrine usual first pressor
SpO2 about 92 to 98%, avoiding both low oxygen and too much
Temperature control: keep below 37.5 °C with strict fever prevention
Glucose 80 to 110

steps.q: Amiodarone infusion after VF. Usual regimen?

options.t: 1 mg/min for 6 hours, then 0.5 mg/min for 18 hours (after the 150 mg load if not already given)
10 mg/min

cases.pearl: **Post ROSC: MAP 65+, SpO2 92 to 98, temp below 37.5, amio 1 then 0.5 mg/min.**

sources.t: AHA Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (2025)
